title: Vector Components and Magnitude
trouble: Students find the direction angle with tan⁻¹ but ignore the quadrant.

blocks.html: A vector can be described by its components or by its length and direction. Switching between the two descriptions is the same as switching between rectangular coordinates and the unit circle, scaled up.

For $\mathbf{v} = \langle a, b \rangle$: magnitude $|\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$; direction angle $\theta$ with $\tan\theta = \frac{b}{a}$, placed in the quadrant of $(a, b)$. Going back: $$\mathbf{v} = \langle |\mathbf{v}|\cos\theta,\ |\mathbf{v}|\sin\theta \rangle.$$ The unit vector in the direction of $\mathbf{v}$ is $\frac{\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{v}|}$.

The magnitude is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs $|a|$ and $|b|$. A vector of length $1$ at angle $\theta$ ends at the unit-circle point $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$; stretching it to length $|\mathbf{v}|$ multiplies both components by $|\mathbf{v}|$.

blocks.name: vectors2d
blocks.cap: Drag the vector into each quadrant and watch the components change sign.

blocks.title: Magnitude and direction
blocks.q: Find the magnitude and direction angle of $\langle -3, 4 \rangle$.
steps: A calculator gives $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{-3}\right) \approx -53.1^\circ$, an angle in Quadrant IV. But $\langle -3, 4 \rangle$ points left and up, into Quadrant II.

blocks.title: From length and angle
blocks.q: A vector has magnitude $10$ and direction angle $150^\circ$. Find its components.

blocks.title: A unit vector
blocks.q: Find the unit vector in the direction of $\langle 5, -12 \rangle$.

blocks.html: Taking the direction from $\tan^{-1}\frac{b}{a}$ without checking the quadrant. $\tan^{-1}$ only gives angles between $-90^\circ$ and $90^\circ$, so for a vector pointing left (negative $a$) you must add $180^\circ$. Sketch the arrow first; the picture tells you the quadrant.
